A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SSR framework, SSR-CoT dataset, and SSRBench benchmark. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, appendices A–F, and checklists are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original dataset-quality measurements, benchmark results, training-stage ablations, latent-representation analysis, and case studies.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds benchmark evaluations, an efficiency comparison, and an alternative-judge evaluation.

M1.justification: The Depth Pro inputs, CLIP/SigLIP encoders, Mamba-based MIDI module, latent projection, training losses, and optional second training stage are retained. Expanded descriptions do not establish a change to the proposed algorithm.

E1.justification: v3 adds evaluation on VSR, What’s Up, VQAv2, TextVQA, POPE, MMBench, and GQA, substantially broadening spatial-relation and general VQA testing. MME evaluation is removed. The training mixture and SpatialBench, SSRBench, and CV-Bench evaluations are retained (Tables 4–5 and Appendix E).

E2.justification: Table 3 and Appendix B add SpatialVLM to the existing comparator set. New Table 7 introduces Qwen2.5-VL fine-tuned on SSR-CoT as a textual-CoT comparator. The other existing benchmark comparators remain.

E3.justification: New protocols substantially extend validation: Table 7 measures tokens per sample, token throughput, and inference latency against an SSR-CoT-fine-tuned control; Table 8 rescores SSRBench using GPT-4o-mini alongside the original Qwen judge. VSR Random and Zero-Shot evaluations are also added. Existing training settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Sections 5.3–5.4 test computational efficiency relative to textual CoT and sensitivity to evaluator-model family. These address questions not experimentally checked in v1. The original second-stage ablation, cosine-similarity visualization, and Appendix F case studies are retained; expanded heatmap explanations do not constitute a new experiment.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Both checklists explicitly acknowledge absent statistical-significance reporting. The additional judge comparison does not introduce statistical uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: v3 adds benchmark, SpatialVLM, efficiency, and alternative-judge results while removing MME results. Table 4 revises SpatialBench averages: Qwen/SSR 3B change from 53.8/59.5 to 59.3/64.8, and 7B from 60.1/63.6 to 64.7/67.0, despite unchanged Table 3 per-task scores. These are revised summaries, not demonstrated performance gains between versions. New Table 7 reports 23.16 seconds/sample for textual CoT versus 0.32 for SSR.

T1.justification: The mathematical architecture descriptions and losses in Equations (1)–(2) are unchanged. Neither version introduces formal theoretical results or proofs; the expanded heatmap discussion adds interpretation rather than mathematical derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction’s contribution list, and conclusion retain the same principal claims about latent spatial reasoning, efficient plug-and-play integration, SSR-CoT, SSRBench, and improved spatial understanding. New experiments support these existing claims without redefining the contributions.

C2.justification: v3 explains how shorter outputs offset slower per-token generation, interprets cross-judge agreement as evidence against model-family bias, and interprets low off-diagonal similarities as sample-specific representations without collapse. The limitation restricting demonstrated applicability to Qwen/Qwen-VL models remains substantively unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 newly specifies the existing quality-control loop’s 10% cache sampling and accuracy-based retention/reannotation procedure. Section 5.5 clarifies token placement in the heatmap comparison, and Appendix E supplies new benchmark sample counts. Existing hyperparameters, hardware, training times, and code/data access statements remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds RoboRefer to related work and adds references supporting the new baseline and benchmarks, including VQASynth and What’s Up; the MME reference is removed. The introduction also redirects a depth-utilization critique from diffusion references to SpatialBot. The overall research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: Changes include localized grammar corrections, expanded quality-control and heatmap explanations, two additional analysis subsections, revised author affiliations, and funding acknowledgments. Most prose and the main section and appendix organization are retained.

P2.justification: v3 adds three substantive tables for general VQA, efficiency, and alternative-judge evaluation; expands comparator tables; and restructures the benchmark-results and dataset-statistics tables. Figure 6 relocates with its discussion. Figure 1 corrects the interpreter label and an example answer; the other illustrations are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens validation of existing claims. Table 7 supplies measurements for the previously unmeasured inference-efficiency claim, while Table 8 shows that SSR’s advantage persists under GPT-4o-mini judging. Broader external evaluations and the SpatialVLM comparison strengthen performance evidence, and the filtering description improves reproducibility. MME results are lost, timing documentation remains limited, and statistical uncertainty is still absent, but the targeted new checks provide a substantial net improvement.
